domanda: Contoso Ltd. manages 400 corporate-owned Windows laptops that are registered in Microsoft Entra ID. The security team wants a group whose membership is populated automatically from the device attribute deviceOwnership so that a Conditional Access policy can target only company-owned hardware. No mailbox or SharePoint site should be created for the group. Which group type and membership type should you select when you create the group?
opzione_a: Group type: Microsoft 365; Membership type: Dynamic Device
opzione_b: Group type: Security; Membership type: Dynamic Device
opzione_c: Group type: Security; Membership type: Dynamic User
opzione_d: Group type: Microsoft 365; Membership type: Assigned
spiegazione: Correct (b): A security group can contain either devices or users, and the Dynamic Device membership type evaluates device attributes such as device.deviceOwnership -eq "Company" to add and remove devices automatically. Security groups have no mailbox or SharePoint site, which satisfies the requirement. Wrong (a): Microsoft 365 groups can include only users as members, so Dynamic Device is not a valid membership type for them. Wrong (c): Dynamic User evaluates user attributes and populates the group with user objects, not devices; a dynamic group can target users or devices, never both. Wrong (d): Assigned membership requires an administrator to add each member manually, which is not automatic, and a Microsoft 365 group cannot contain devices and does provision a mailbox and SharePoint site. Correction: url_riferimento was a bare page link and has been replaced with the #group-types deep link that actually carries the membership statements. Note that device-based dynamic membership groups can only be created with the rule syntax text box, because the rule builder supports user-based groups only.
tags: microsoft entra id,groups,security group,microsoft 365 group,dynamic device,membership type

domanda: An administrator opens the dynamic membership rule builder in the Microsoft Entra admin center to configure a Dynamic User group. What is the maximum number of expressions the rule builder supports before the rule must be authored in the rule syntax text box instead?
spiegazione: Correct (b): Microsoft Learn states that the rule builder supports the construction of up to five expressions; a rule with more than five expressions is explicitly listed as requiring the rule syntax text box. Wrong (a): Three is not the documented limit; the builder accepts more than three expressions. Wrong (c): Ten is not a documented rule builder limit for dynamic membership rules. Wrong (d): 15 is not the expression limit. It is easily confused with the 15 extensionAttribute properties (extensionAttribute1-15) that are supported in dynamic rules, and with the 15,000 dynamic membership groups a single tenant can have.

domanda: You download the bulk upload CSV template from Microsoft Entra ID > Users > Bulk create. You plan to create 60 new internal user accounts. Which set of columns must contain a value in every data row for the file to pass validation?
opzione_a: Name [displayName], User name [userPrincipalName], Initial password [passwordProfile], Block sign in (Yes/No) [accountEnabled]
opzione_b: Name [displayName], User name [userPrincipalName], First name [givenName], Last name [surname]
opzione_c: User name [userPrincipalName], Initial password [passwordProfile], Usage location [usageLocation], Department [department]
opzione_d: Name [displayName], User name [userPrincipalName], Initial password [passwordProfile], Usage location [usageLocation]
spiegazione: Correct (a): Microsoft Learn states that only the first four columns of the bulk create template are required: Name, User name (userPrincipalName), Initial password, and Block sign in (Yes/No). All other columns are optional and can be left empty. Wrong (b): First name and Last name are optional properties in the template, and Initial password and Block sign in are missing from this set. Wrong (c): Usage location and Department are optional, and this set omits the required Name and Block sign in columns. Wrong (d): Usage location is optional; the fourth required column is Block sign in (Yes/No), which maps to accountEnabled. Note that the version:v1.0 row and the column header row must be preserved exactly as downloaded or the upload cannot be processed, the examples row must be removed, and bulk create requires at least the User Administrator role.
tags: microsoft entra id,bulk create,csv template,users,required columns

domanda: You are documenting what can be a member of each Microsoft Entra group type for your organization's identity standards. Which of the following membership scenarios are supported? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: A device object can be a member of a security group.
opzione_b: A device object can be a member of a Microsoft 365 group.
opzione_c: A service principal can be a member of a security group.
opzione_d: A security group can be added as a member of a Microsoft 365 group.
opzione_e: A security group can be added as a member of another security group.
spiegazione: Correct (a): Microsoft Learn states that members of a security group can include users, devices, and service principals. Correct (c): Service principals are explicitly listed as supported members of a security group; users and service principals can also own a security group. Correct (e): For the security group type you can add an existing group to another group (nested groups). Nesting is supported for membership and Conditional Access scopes, but members of the nested child group do not gain access to shared resources and applications assigned to the parent group, and licenses cannot be applied to nested security groups. Wrong (b): Members of a Microsoft 365 group can only include users, so devices cannot be added. Wrong (d): Adding security groups to Microsoft 365 groups is explicitly listed as unsupported, as is adding Microsoft 365 groups to security groups or to other Microsoft 365 groups. Correction: sotto_argomento was "Manage external users", which did not match a question about group types, and has been set to "Create users and groups". The explanation of option (e) previously said members of the parent group gain access; it has been rewritten to state the documented behavior, that nested groups do not gain access to resources assigned to the parent.
tags: microsoft entra id,group types,security group,microsoft 365 group,nested groups,service principal

domanda: Fabrikam Inc. is a partner organization with its own Microsoft Entra tenant. Contoso must give 200 Fabrikam employees access to a Contoso line-of-business application. The Fabrikam employees must sign in with their existing Fabrikam credentials, and each must receive an invitation email. A Contoso administrator has a CSV file that lists the 200 email addresses. Which action should the administrator perform?
opzione_a: In Microsoft Entra ID, go to Users > Bulk create and upload the CSV file.
opzione_b: In Microsoft Entra ID, go to Users > Bulk operations > Bulk invite and upload the CSV file.
opzione_c: Open the target group, select Members > Bulk operations > Import members, and upload the CSV file.
opzione_d: In Microsoft Entra ID, go to Users > Bulk create, upload the CSV file, and then change the UserType of each new account to Guest.
spiegazione: Correct (b): Bulk invite (Users > Bulk operations > Bulk invite) is the documented way to invite external B2B collaboration users from a CSV file and send them invitation emails. The template requires the Email address to invite [inviteeEmail] and Redirection url columns. Invited B2B users authenticate with credentials from their home identity provider, are created with UserType set to Guest, and receive a UPN in the form emailaddress#EXT#@domain. Wrong (a): Microsoft Learn explicitly states that the bulk create operation creates internal member accounts with the passwords specified in the CSV file and that no invitation emails are sent; the users would sign in with Contoso credentials, not Fabrikam credentials. Wrong (c): Bulk import members only adds objects that already exist in the directory to a group, referenced by object ID or UPN. It does not create or invite any user. Wrong (d): Changing UserType to Guest only changes the user's stated relationship to the organization and has no relation to how the user signs in, so these accounts would still be internal accounts with Contoso credentials and no invitation would be sent. Correction: option (b) previously read "Users > Bulk invite"; the documented navigation is Users > Bulk operations > Bulk invite, and the option text has been corrected to match the portal.
tags: microsoft entra id,b2b collaboration,bulk invite,guest users,usertype,external identities

domanda: Northwind Traders wants a Dynamic User security group that contains every internal employee in the tenant but excludes all B2B collaboration guests. The group must stay accurate as employees join and leave. Which membership rule should you configure?
spiegazione: Correct (b): Microsoft Learn documents this exact pattern. The rule user.objectId -ne null selects all users, and combining it with user.userType -eq "Member" restricts membership to member users and excludes guests. Wrong (a): This is the documented "all users" rule, but Learn explicitly states it adds both business-to-business guest users and member users, so guests would not be excluded. Wrong (c): The userType property allows the values member, guest, and null. A rule that only tests -ne "Guest" would also match user objects whose userType is null, so it does not reliably select just internal members. Wrong (d): Putting null in quotation marks makes it a literal string comparison. Learn states you should use quotation marks around the word null only if you want it interpreted as a literal string value; the correct null check is user.objectId -ne null without quotes.

domanda: A sales manager whose user object ID is aaaaaaaa-0000-1111-2222-bbbbbbbbbbbb needs a group that always contains the people who report directly to her. The Manager property is correctly populated for all users in the tenant. Which membership rule should you enter for the Dynamic User group?
spiegazione: Correct (a): Microsoft Learn documents the direct reports rule syntax as Direct Reports for "{objectID_of_manager}", where the value is the object ID of the manager. This rule must be authored in the rule syntax text box because the rule builder does not support it, and note that the manager is also added to the group. Wrong (b): manager is not listed among the supported user properties for building a single-expression dynamic membership rule; the documented mechanism for direct reports is the dedicated Direct Reports for syntax. Wrong (c): The direct reports rule requires the manager's object ID, which you find in the manager's profile, not a user principal name or email address. Wrong (d): Learn explicitly states that you can't combine the direct reports rule with any other membership rules. It also supports only the manager's direct reports, not the reports of those reports. Correction: option (d) previously used the unsupported user.manager property, which made it a duplicate of the flaw in option (b) rather than testing the documented "cannot be combined with other rules" restriction. It has been rewritten to use the correct Direct Reports for syntax combined with a second expression, so it is now wrong for exactly one clear reason.
tags: microsoft entra id,dynamic membership,direct reports,membership rule,manager

domanda: Your organization is standardizing how administrators author dynamic membership rules. You need to identify which rules cannot be created with the rule builder in the Microsoft Entra admin center and must be authored in the rule syntax text box. Which rules require the text box? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: A rule that combines six expressions with the -and and -or operators.
opzione_b: A rule that uses the Direct Reports for "{objectID_of_manager}" syntax.
opzione_c: A rule that uses the -notContains operator.
opzione_d: A single-expression rule such as user.department -eq "Sales".
opzione_e: A two-expression rule that uses the -startsWith operator on user.displayName.
spiegazione: Correct (a): Microsoft Learn lists a rule with more than five expressions as requiring the text box, because the rule builder supports only up to five expressions. Correct (b): A rule for direct reports is explicitly listed as requiring the text box. Correct (c): A rule with a -contains or -notContains operator is explicitly listed as requiring the text box. Wrong (d): A single simple expression is exactly the kind of rule the rule builder is designed for. Wrong (e): Two expressions is well within the five-expression limit and -startsWith is a standard operator the rule builder handles. Other documented text-box-only cases include setting operator precedence, complex expressions such as (user.proxyAddresses -any (_ -startsWith "contoso")), and all device-based dynamic membership groups, since the rule builder is available only for user-based groups.
tags: microsoft entra id,dynamic membership,rule builder,rule syntax,operators,direct reports

domanda: Adatum Corporation collaborates with several partner firms whose users have been invited into the Adatum tenant through B2B collaboration. You must create a group that always contains every guest user in the tenant so that a Conditional Access policy can target them. The group must not provision a mailbox or a SharePoint site, and membership must never be maintained by hand. Select the appropriate option for each dropdown.
opzione_b: Membership type: [Assigned | Dynamic User | Dynamic Device]
opzione_d: Minimum license required for each unique member: [Microsoft Entra ID Free | Microsoft Entra ID P1 | Microsoft Entra ID P2]
spiegazione: Group type = Security: Security groups are used to manage access to shared resources and do not provision a mailbox or SharePoint site, unlike Microsoft 365 groups. Mail-enabled security groups cannot be managed in the Microsoft Entra admin center at all; Learn states they can only be managed in the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft 365 admin center. Membership type = Dynamic User: Guests are user objects, and only Dynamic User membership evaluates user attributes automatically. Assigned would require manual maintenance, and Dynamic Device evaluates device attributes only. Membership rule = user.userType -eq "Guest": userType is a supported string property whose allowed values are member, guest, and null, and Guest indicates a user who is not internal to the company. user.objectId -ne null is the documented "all users" rule that adds both guests and members, and device.deviceOwnership is a device attribute that cannot be used in a user rule. Minimum license = Microsoft Entra ID P1: Learn states dynamic membership groups require a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license (or an Intune for Education license) for each unique user who is a member of one or more dynamic membership groups, and that you must hold enough licenses to cover all such users even though you do not have to assign them. Microsoft Entra ID Free does not include the feature, and P2 exceeds the documented minimum.
tags: microsoft entra id,dynamic membership,usertype,guest,licensing,entra id p1,security group

domanda: Contoso has an existing Microsoft Entra security group named Sales-All. The group was created with the Membership type set to Assigned, and the option "Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group" was left set to No. You sign in as a Groups Administrator. For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No. 1) You can change the membership type of Sales-All from Assigned to Dynamic User. 2) After Sales-All is changed to Dynamic User, you can still manually add a specific user to the group from the Members page. 3) You can change the group type of Sales-All from Security to Microsoft 365.
opzione_a: You can change the membership type of Sales-All from Assigned to Dynamic User.
opzione_b: After Sales-All is changed to Dynamic User, you can still manually add a specific user to the group from the Members page.
opzione_c: You can change the group type of Sales-All from Security to Microsoft 365.
spiegazione: Statement 1 = Yes: On the group's Properties page you can edit the group name, description, and Membership type. Microsoft Learn states the membership type can be changed and that it is locked only if the "Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group" option was enabled, which is not the case here. The Groups Administrator role is sufficient to edit group settings. Statement 2 = No: Learn explicitly states that you can't manually add or remove a member of a dynamic membership group. Membership is determined solely by evaluating the membership rule against user or device attributes. Statement 3 = No: Learn explicitly states that you can't change the type of a group after it's been created. To change the Group type you must delete the group and create a new one.
tags: microsoft entra id,groups,membership type,group type,dynamic membership,group properties

domanda: An administrator at Fabrikam is authoring membership rules for Dynamic Device security groups in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Devices are enrolled in Microsoft Intune, and a mix of Microsoft Entra joined, Microsoft Entra hybrid joined, and Microsoft Entra registered devices exists in the tenant. For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No. 1) The rule device.deviceOwnership -eq "Corporate" adds the company-owned devices to the group. 2) The rule device.deviceTrustType -eq "ServerAD" adds the Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices to the group. 3) A Dynamic Device rule can reference the department attribute of the device's registered owner.
opzione_a: The rule device.deviceOwnership -eq "Corporate" adds the company-owned devices to the group.
opzione_b: The rule device.deviceTrustType -eq "ServerAD" adds the Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices to the group.
opzione_c: A Dynamic Device rule can reference the department attribute of the device's registered owner.
spiegazione: Statement 1 = No: This is the classic Intune trap. Microsoft Learn states that when you use deviceOwnership to create dynamic membership groups for devices, you need to set the value equal to "Company". The allowed values are Personal, Company, and Unknown. Intune represents the same ownership as Corporate in its own reporting, but the dynamic rule must use Company. Statement 2 = Yes: For deviceTrustType, Learn documents AzureAD to represent Microsoft Entra joined devices, ServerAD to represent Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices, and Workplace to represent Microsoft Entra registered devices. Statement 3 = No: Learn explicitly states you can't create a device membership group based on the user attributes of the device owner; device membership rules can reference only device attributes. A single dynamic group can target users or devices, never both.

domanda: A helpdesk technician reports that a Dynamic User group intended to contain "every user who has any value in the Department field" is returning zero members, even though hundreds of users clearly have a department populated. The current membership rule is user.department -ne "null". You must correct the rule. Which membership rule should you configure?
spiegazione: Correct (a): Microsoft Learn states that to specify a null value in a rule you use -eq or -ne when comparing the null value, and gives user.mail -ne null as the correct way to reference the null value, without quotation marks. The original rule failed because quotation marks around null make it a literal string comparison, so it only matched users whose department was literally the text "null". Wrong (b): -notContains performs a partial string match and is not the documented way to perform a null check; Learn also cautions to minimize the use of Match and Contains operators because they slow dynamic group processing. Wrong (c): Learn explicitly states you must not use the -not operator as a comparative operator for the null value, and that doing so returns an error whether you use null or $null. Wrong (d): -match and -notMatch are regular expression operators and, with null in quotation marks, this again compares against the literal string "null" rather than performing a null check.
tags: microsoft entra id,dynamic membership,null values,troubleshooting,membership rule,operators

domanda: Litware Inc. uses the following membership rule on a Dynamic User security group. No parentheses are present in the rule: user.country -eq "US" -and user.department -eq "Marketing" -or user.department -eq "Sales". Based on the documented operator precedence for dynamic membership rules, determine whether each user is added to the group. Select the appropriate option for each dropdown.
opzione_a: A user whose country is US and whose department is Marketing: [Added | Not added]
opzione_b: A user whose country is Canada and whose department is Sales: [Added | Not added]
opzione_c: A user whose country is Canada and whose department is Marketing: [Added | Not added]
opzione_d: A user whose country is US and whose department is Finance: [Added | Not added]
spiegazione: Microsoft Learn documents operator precedence from highest to lowest as: the comparison operators (-eq, -ne, -startsWith, -notStartsWith, -contains, -notContains, -match, -notMatch, -in, -notIn), then -not, then -and, then -or, then -any and -all. Because -and binds more tightly than -or, the rule is evaluated as (user.country -eq "US" -and user.department -eq "Marketing") -or (user.department -eq "Sales"). Dropdown 1 = Added: The user satisfies both halves of the -and branch. Dropdown 2 = Added: The -or branch is satisfied by department Sales on its own; country is irrelevant to that branch, which is the common misreading of this rule. Dropdown 3 = Not added: The -and branch fails because country is not US, and the -or branch fails because the department is not Sales. Dropdown 4 = Not added: The -and branch fails on department, and the -or branch fails on department. Learn notes you need parentheses only when the default precedence doesn't meet your requirements. Writing user.country -eq "US" -and (user.department -eq "Marketing" -or user.department -eq "Sales") would instead require US for every member and would exclude the Canadian Sales user, and setting operator precedence explicitly is one of the cases that requires the rule syntax text box rather than the rule builder. Correction: the final sentence previously asserted only that parentheses "would change the result" without saying how; it now states the specific alternate grouping and which user it excludes.
tags: microsoft entra id,dynamic membership,operator precedence,membership rule,and,or

domanda: Woodgrove Bank has a Microsoft Entra ID P1 tenant containing a security group named Helpdesk-Team. The group was created with Membership type set to Dynamic User and a rule of user.jobTitle -eq "Helpdesk Analyst". You must assign the Helpdesk Administrator Microsoft Entra role to the group so that all of its members inherit the role. You sign in as a Privileged Role Administrator, but the group does not appear as an available option when you try to assign the role. You must resolve the issue while keeping the number of administrative steps to a minimum. What should you do?
opzione_a: Create a new security group, set "Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group" to Yes, set the Membership type to Assigned, add the analysts as members, and assign the Helpdesk Administrator role to the new group.
opzione_b: Edit the properties of Helpdesk-Team and set the isAssignableToRole property to true by using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
opzione_c: Change the Membership type of Helpdesk-Team from Dynamic User to Assigned, and then assign the Helpdesk Administrator role to the group.
opzione_d: Add Helpdesk-Team as a nested member of a new role-assignable security group, and then assign the Helpdesk Administrator role to the parent group.
spiegazione: Correct (a): To assign a Microsoft Entra role to a group, the group must have been created with isAssignableToRole set to true (the "Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group" option). Microsoft Learn states this property can only be set on new groups, that it is immutable, that you can't make an existing group a role-assignable group, and that the membership type for role-assignable groups must be Assigned and can't be a dynamic group. Creating a new group with both settings correct is therefore the only supported path, and it requires at least the Privileged Role Administrator role, which you already have. In the portal, enabling the option automatically selects Assigned as the Membership type. Wrong (b): The isAssignableToRole property can only be set on new groups and is immutable once the group is created, so this fails regardless of the tool used. Wrong (c): Changing the membership type to Assigned does not make the group role-assignable. The group still has isAssignableToRole set to false and that value cannot be changed after creation. Wrong (d): Group nesting isn't supported for role-assignable groups; Learn states a group can't be added as a member of a role-assignable group.
tags: microsoft entra id,role-assignable group,isassignabletorole,dynamic membership,privileged role administrator,troubleshooting

domanda: Your security team is reviewing the design constraints of role-assignable Microsoft Entra groups before rolling them out. Which statements about role-assignable groups are true? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: The membership type of a role-assignable group must be Assigned.
opzione_b: The isAssignableToRole property can be enabled on an existing group that was created without it.
opzione_c: You must be assigned at least the Privileged Role Administrator role to create a role-assignable group.
opzione_d: A group cannot be added as a member of a role-assignable group.
opzione_e: A maximum of 5,000 role-assignable groups can be created in a single tenant.
spiegazione: Correct (a): Microsoft Learn states the membership type for role-assignable groups must be Assigned and can't be a Microsoft Entra dynamic group, because automated population of dynamic membership groups could lead to an unwanted account being added to the group and thus assigned the role. Correct (c): Learn states you must be assigned at least the Privileged Role Administrator role to create a role-assignable group. Correct (d): Group nesting isn't supported; a group can't be added as a member of a role-assignable group. Wrong (b): The isAssignableToRole property can only be set on new groups and is immutable. Learn explicitly states you can't make an existing group a role-assignable group. Wrong (e): The documented limit is a maximum of 500 role-assignable groups in a single Microsoft Entra organization, not 5,000. Note also that the feature requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license, that a role-assignable group can be either a security group or a Microsoft 365 group, and that Microsoft Graph requires the RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory permission (Group.ReadWrite.All is not sufficient) to manage the membership of such a group.
